title: Dispatch BBA 3: Patients Seen at Windows of a Demolished Ward
summary: The market remained open as the dates in the register came due.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A woman in a white apron appeared at an upper window above the market yesterday morning. There is no building at that height. Several vendors recognized her as Sister Kells from photographs in the municipal archive.

Elsewhere in the square, a boy with a bandaged arm asked a vendor for the east ward. When the vendor explained that the hospital was gone, the boy replied that he had been told to report at noon. He was not seen again after the bell sounded.

At 5:40, the bell gave six strokes, the same as on its first morning. The Institute's cylinder again captured the sound. On playback, the recording included voices beneath the bell: a woman giving directions, the movement of wheels, and a child coughing.

Three new names appeared in the register after noon. They belong to people living in Alderwick today. None has reported feeling unwell. All three were born within two streets of the former hospital boundary.

Dr. Saye has asked the city to close the market for one day. The council has agreed to close the central square between 5:00 and 7:00 this morning while the Institute examines the site with a full lens assembly.
